result.summary: Handles socket error conditions in the P2P network loop and HTTP server separately from read events. When `poll()` reports socket errors or hangups on connections where reads are not currently requested, the node disconnects immediately instead of attempting an I/O operation that would inevitably fail. It also adds functional test coverage for TCP urgent data handling and peer resets while sending.
result.problem: When socket polling reports an error condition on a connection whose reads are paused, the node attempts a write (or read in HTTP) that subsequently fails and triggers a disconnect anyway. This produces inaccurate log messages and redundant failed I/O calls.
evidence: PR description: 'If errorSet is reported for a socket we did not request to read from, disconnect directly instead. This just adds clarity: previously it would attempt a send that would then fail. The only side-effect is a changed log message.'
Commit 582840ae83: 'Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP when no read was requested, skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect the peer.'
result.scope_notes: This PR is stacked on PR #36716 and incorporates its commits. Most of the diff consists of functional test framework additions and new test cases for TCP urgent data and socket resets.
result.card: Disconnects sockets immediately when poll() reports error or hangup events on connections where reads were not requested, rather than attempting a doomed send or read first. This applies to both the P2P networking loop and the HTTP server, avoiding redundant failed I/O operations and clarifying debug log output upon disconnection. It also expands test coverage for TCP urgent data handling and peer resets during send stalls. Depends on PR #36716.

risk.why: A logic error in socket event handling could prematurely drop healthy P2P or RPC connections or fail to clean up dead sockets.
